name: crypto-hmac384
algorithm: std HMAC-SHA384 (RFC 2104) of every 64-byte message of splitmix64 bytes under a 48-byte key, the key's first byte xored with each tag's, reps passes (mk/crypto-hmac384.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard MAC
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no HMAC; the hmac crate is third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Work per step: one HMAC-SHA384 of a 64-byte message under a 48-byte key, the one-shot form each library offers: Mk crypto.Hmac384, Go hmac.New(sha512.New384, key) then Write and Sum, Zig HmacSha384.create. Four SHA-512 compressions per message (the two pad blocks, the message with its padding, the outer hash); no column keeps the pads' states across messages. Messages per second = mib * 16384 * reps / median.
Go: crypto/sha512 computes the message schedule with AVX2 on amd64 when the CPU has it, whatever GOAMD64 says; Mk's SHA-512 is scalar (std-hash2's hash-sha384 notes).

Checksums from the go column (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off, Go 1.27, owner's machine, 2026-11-12); the Mk column (mk build --release, mk from the tree) printed the same at both arg sets. Written by the std-crypto2 lane. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
